title: Asteron Systems — Ecosystem Integration & GPU Edge Strategy
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and Asteron to scope an edge GPU onramp integration. Discussed deployment models (hosted vs dedicated vs private), security requirements, high-level architecture, and next steps for a benchmark pilot. Action items assigned for integration spec, security docs, and sandbox access.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-08 16:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luca Moretti (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Asteron Head Partnerships), Tom Becker (Asteron CTO), Elena Martens (Platform Eng), Diego Ramos (Infra)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be incomplete): Intro / discovery for partner onramp integration. Customer is exploring a hybrid edge GPU routing to support inference workloads embedded in their SI products. Security & private deployment are high priority.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for making the time. Maya from Redwood here, I'll kick us off. Quick intro?
[00:12] Priya Rao: Hi all, Priya. We're excited to explore how Redwood could fit into Asteron's ecosystem. We partner with a few SI's that need small-footprint GPU inference at the edge.
[00:22] Tom Becker: Tom here, CTO. Main concerns are predictable latency, throughput, and making sure data never leaks to third party unless encrypted and audited.
[00:35] Luca Moretti: Great, thanks Tom. Quick note on Redwood side: we run hosted API, dedicated capacity, and private deployments — but for partner onramp most folks want either dedicated pools or VPC private deploy.
[00:50] Elena Martens: Quick clarification, when you say private deploy do you mean full on-prem or VPC-hosted control plane?
[00:57] Luca Moretti: Both. We have a private control plane option that sits inside customer VPCs and an on-prem package for air-gapped installs. There are tradeoffs on updates and telemetry obviously.
[01:10] Diego Ramos: When you say telemetry what gets sent back? We can't send customer PII or payloads off network.
[01:17] Samir Patel: By default we collect basic metrics — token counts, latency histograms, error rates. Payloads can be configured to not leave the VPC; we integrate with KMS/HSM for key management and provide audit logs.
[01:30] Priya Rao: Ok good. Compliance: SOC2 is a must, maybe ISO later. Do you have SOC2 report, and can you support our auditors?
[01:40] Maya Chen: Yes we have SOC2 Type II; I'll share the package. We also have an enterprise compliance pack we can hand to your auditors. Link: https://redwood.ai/security/pack (note: placeholder link)
[01:52] Tom Becker: Perfect. For the bench, our SI partners will test with small sequence length models — 2/3 different model sizes — plus a quantized 4-bit variant. Any advice?
[02:06] Luca Moretti: Sounds in line with what we see. On quantized models, we recommend testing both 4-bit and 8-bit for quality vs latency tradeoffs. Our runtime does kernel selection per architecture; that can affect throughput a lot.
[02:20] Diego Ramos: Which GPUs are you validating? We run a mix of A100s in the core and Jetson/RTX A2000-ish on the edge.
[02:29] Luca Moretti: Core: A100 and H100 are validated. For edge, we often use T4/RTX series and partnerships for mobile accelerators. There will be some perf differences but we can map model profiles to best-fit runtimes.
[02:42] Priya Rao: For partner workflow, we'd like Redwood to expose an API or SDK so our SIs can onboard models without learning a whole new infra.
[02:52] Maya Chen: Absolutely, we have SDKs and a model catalog. Also an integration pattern doc that outlines routing, canary rollouts, and fallback to cheaper variants. I'll include that doc.
[03:04] Tom Becker: How do you route requests for latency sensitive stuff? For some customer flows 50 ms p90 is critical.
[03:12] Luca Moretti: We can route by policy: latency-first routing will favor local edge pools, otherwise cost-first will go to pooled capacity. We also have automatic fallback which can route to a smaller model if SLOs are at risk.
[03:26] Elena Martens: That fallback — is it transparent to caller or does it return a different model id? We need deterministic outputs for some compliance reasons.
[03:36] Samir Patel: Good point. Fallbacks are configurable: you can force strict model pinning (no fallback), or allow fallback with explicit model metadata in the response so the caller knows which variant served the request.
[03:50] Priya Rao: Timeline wise — we're thinking of a Q1 partner pilot with 2 SIs. What's a realistic pilot scope?
[03:59] Maya Chen: Typical is 2 weeks of benching plus a 4-week pilot in production-like traffic. For discovery we can do a 10k synthetic qps test to measure tail latency and cost.
[04:12] Diego Ramos: 10k qps seems big for edge — maybe smaller per-node but aggregated. Will you benchmark end-to-end including our network overlay?
[04:21] Luca Moretti: Yes we'd prefer full-stack benchmarks: client, edge node, and backend. We can use your overlay if you provide sandbox VPC access.
[04:32] Tom Becker: Security again — encryption at rest + in transit, KMS, and audit logs are required. Also we need RBAC integrated with our Okta SSO.
[04:42] Samir Patel: We support SAML/SSO via Okta, role-based access controls, and integrate with customer KMS providers. We'll send you SSO integration docs.
[04:52] Priya Rao: Any commercial model for partners? Revenue share or referral?
[04:57] Maya Chen: We have partner programs, reseller margins, and joint go-to-market. For pilots we usually cover initial infra credits and then discuss committed capacity pricing for Dedicated.
[05:08] Elena Martens: Let's talk about integration mechanics — do you provide Terraform modules or Helm charts?
[05:14] Luca Moretti: For VPC installs we provide Terraform modules, and for on-prem we have Helm charts plus an appliance bundle. We'll share the repo.
[05:24] Tom Becker: Latency numbers — what can we expect on small edge GPUs for a 2k token sequence?
[05:31] Luca Moretti: Ballpark: on small inference optimized models we see 80–200 ms p95 on T4-class hardware for shorter sequences; long 2k sequences will of course be higher. Exact numbers depend on batching and KV cache use.
[05:45] Diego Ramos: KV cache — the custome spelling heard previously — is your KV cache sharable across pods? We need stateful caches for multi-turn chat.
[05:54] Samir Patel: Our KV cache can be sticky per instance or shared via fast in-memory clusters. For edge we often recommend local sticky caches to avoid cross-node latency.
[06:07] Priya Rao: Any limits on model size / context length? Some SI partners use 8k+ context.
[06:14] Luca Moretti: We support long-context models; runtime selection again matters. For very long contexts we recommend partitioned KV and streaming responses to keep memory bounded.
[06:25] Tom Becker: When you say streaming, do you handle partial responses and reassembly? Clients expect chunked responses.
[06:32] Samir Patel: Yes we support streaming over the API and also provide function-calling style structured outputs. There may be small differences in behaviour between Hosted and Private modes, we'll doc that.
[06:45] Maya Chen: I'm going to pause here and ask — are there any blockers that would prevent Asteron from piloting with Redwood?
[06:53] Priya Rao: Auditability and legal are minor — we need to review the data processing addendum. Also procurement will want a limit on liability for pilot.
[07:03] Maya Chen: Understood. We'll share the DPA and an abbreviated contract for pilot usage.
[07:10] Tom Becker: Network-wise, we sometimes have NAT constraints at customer edge sites — will Redwood's client SDK handle NAT traversal or do we need dedicated tunnels?
[07:20] Luca Moretti: SDKs typically work over HTTPS outbound, which is NAT-friendly. For private peering/low latency we can set up direct connect or tunnels as needed.
[07:33] Diego Ramos: Ok. Let's talk about provisioning — how does Redwood handle autoscaling for edge pools?
[07:40] Samir Patel: We support policy-driven autoscaling with thresholding by CPU/GPU and queue-length, and burst capacity for sudden load spikes. For edge nodes we recommend conservative scaling to avoid cold starts.
[07:54] Priya Rao: Cold starts: our SI partners will batch inference in store devices — they can't tolerate multi-second cold starts.
[08:02] Luca Moretti: We have warm-pool strategies and pre-warmed containers for critical endpoints. That reduces cold start to sub-100 ms in many cases for small models.
[08:13] Tom Becker: Are there observability hooks we can expose to our partners? We need token-level billing and per-route latency breakdowns.
[08:21] Maya Chen: Redwood Console exposes per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost, and tracing. We can provide read-only dashboards to partners if you want.
[08:33] Elena Martens: We'd like alerting integration with PagerDuty.
[08:36] Samir Patel: We integrate with PagerDuty, Datadog, and Prometheus. We'll include sample alert rules.
[08:44] Priya Rao: How about model governance? If SI partners upload custom models, who is responsible for model cataloging and access control?
[08:53] Luca Moretti: We support org-level catalogs. Partners can have separate namespaces and RBAC controls. There's also model signing/verification if you want to enforce provenance.
[09:04] Tom Becker: Model signing — can you enforce that only signed models go to production?
[09:08] Samir Patel: Yes, enforcement policies can be set so unsigned artifacts are rejected.
[09:12] Maya Chen: Quick note — I uploaded a short partner deck earlier; I'll email the link after this call. Anything else on compliance or deployment?
[09:21] Priya Rao: One ask: we need data residency in EU for some customers; can you pin regions per tenant?
[09:28] Luca Moretti: Yes, routing policies can pin region and we support EU-only deployments. For private installs you control the region entirely.
[09:37] Elena Martens: On cost modelling, can Redwood provide unit-cost estimates per 1k tokens for different runtimes? Our procurement will ask.
[09:45] Maya Chen: Yes we'll provide tokenized cost models and a cost calculator for Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private.
[09:53] Tom Becker: About SLOs — do you offer SLA-backed latency guarantees for Dedicated?
[09:58] Samir Patel: For Dedicated plans we offer SLA-backed uptime and latency targets, yes. We'll share sample SLA language.
[10:08] Priya Rao: Great. For the pilot we want two benchmarks: latency-focused and cost-focused.
[10:15] Luca Moretti: We'll draft a perf checklist. Suggestion: 1) latency bench with p95/p99 targets; 2) cost bench measuring tokens/cost tradeoffs across quantization and batching configs.
[10:28] Diego Ramos: For batching: if we batch on edge how do you handle multi-tenant isolation? We can't allow cross-tenant model leakage in batch.
[10:36] Samir Patel: Batching is always tenant-aware. We keep tenant affinity and model isolation; cross-tenant mixing won't happen.
[10:44] Maya Chen: Ok sprinting forward — I will send an initial integration spec and security pack. Luca, can you own the perf checklist?
[10:52] Luca Moretti: Yep I'll own that and will include suggested quantization profiles.
[10:56] Priya Rao: Procurement will require an initial MOU. We'll loop in legal after the partner package.
[11:04] Tom Becker: One more technical: what about KV cache durability for multi-turn state if edge node fails?
[11:12] Luca Moretti: For durability you can persist checkpoints to a fast store; for edge we sometimes accept ephemeral caches with periodic snapshot replication to a regional store. We'll outline the options in the spec.
[11:26] Diego Ramos: Sounds good. Can you also include a runbook for failover? Our SIs want to integrate into their orchestration.
[11:33] Samir Patel: We'll add a failover runbook and example SRE playbook to the deck.
[11:41] Priya Rao: Any red flags from Redwood side about partnering with Asteron?
[11:45] Maya Chen: None so far; just need to validate legal and network constraints.
[11:50] Tom Becker: Ok, next steps recap?
[11:54] Maya Chen: We'll send: 1) partner integration deck + security pack, 2) DPA and pilot contract template, 3) perf checklist — Luca will own, 4) request sandbox VPC access from Diego.
[12:09] Priya Rao: We'll provide: 1) compliance contacts, 2) list of SI partner workloads and model sizes, 3) sandbox VPC details.
[12:20] Maya Chen: Great. I'll follow up with a Calendly for the technical deep dive.
[12:26] Tom Becker: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the perf checklist.
[12:30] Maya Chen: Thanks all, talk soon.

(End of call)

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts — e.g., "K V cash" appears in a few spots instead of "KV cache"; product names sometimes abbreviated as "Redwood Dedicate" instead of "Dedicated". Shared artifacts referenced: partner deck (will be emailed), perf checklist (to be shared in repo), security pack link (above).
